body:
Can you share the config you're using? Do you have the object-shorthand rule turned on? With the information you provided, it looks like you're not using the object shorthand syntax and, assuming you have the rule turned on in your config, this warning is the expected behavior. The shorthand notation would be:

``` js
const constant = 'foo'
const obj = { 
  constant
}
```
@kaicataldo Look again at the example. The property name is computed.
Ah, I see. Shouldn't be doing this so late.

Updated my original comment to add the configuration part that is responsible for object-shorthand. I do not see any issue here. I only encountered this after upgrading to 2.9.0 and I suspect it is related to this [e2ad1ec](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/commit/e2ad1ec7f6e48f8f4ab9014e5562ec168d9d2442)

issue.body:
**What version/configuration are you using?**

`package.json`

``` json
{
  "name": "eslint-object-shorthand-bug",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "",
  "main": "index.js",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "eslint ."
  },
  "author": "",
  "license": "ISC",
  "devDependencies": {
    "babel-eslint": "^6.0.4",
    "eslint": "^2.9.0",
    "eslint-config-airbnb": "^9.0.1",
    "eslint-plugin-import": "^1.8.0"
  },
  "eslintConfig": {
    "extends": "airbnb/base",
    "parser": "babel-eslint"
  }
}
```

`repro.js`

``` javascript
export default function addType(obj, type) {
  return Object.assign({ [type]: type }, obj);
}
```

**What did you do?**

`npm test`

**What happened?**

``` bash
> eslint-object-shorthand-bug@1.0.0 test /home/mmyrseth/try-bin/js/eslint
> eslint .


~/eslint-object-shorthand-bug/repro.js
  2:26  error  Expected property shorthand  object-shorthand

✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)

npm ERR! Test failed.  See above for more details.
```

**What did you expect to happen?**

The object shorthand is intended to simplify cases where you have object literals like the following: `{ type: type }` where you can replace it with simply: `{ type }`. However, this has a completely different meaning than what's intended with the computed/dynamic property names: `{ [type]: type }`. Here we do not want to set the key "type", but the key whose name is contained in the `type` variable (and we want to set the value to the same thing, so `key === value`).
